Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_learning), [Source Data](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_data).
- [The Awful Truth: Learning Facts That Favor the Other Side](https://gsood.com/research/papers/otherpk.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-awful-truth-learning-facts-that-favor-the-other-side/)): With Robert C. Luskin. Across 14 Deliberative Polls, participants became more accurate about facts that challenged their initial positions in 13 studies. Gains on these facts exceeded gains on congenial facts in 11 studies, but only two conditional intervals excluded zero. The comparisons describe learning across initial positions; they do not identify a causal effect of deliberation or distinguish motivated learning from initial knowledge, response behavior, and room to improve. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_otherpk), [Source Data](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_data).
- [Deliberation and Misinformation](https://gsood.com/research/papers/deliberation_misinformation.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/deliberation-and-misinformation/)): With Robert C. Luskin. Across 19 misinformation-type items in seven Deliberative Polls, incorrect answers fell from 23% to 10%, and participants who began wrong were as likely to end right as those who began not knowing. In polls with control groups, attending cut overestimates of the number of undocumented immigrants by 15 points, but reduced confident denial of human-caused warming only slightly and not durably. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_misinformation).
- [Deliberative Distortions? Homogenization, Polarization, and Domination in Small Group Deliberations](https://gsood.com/research/papers/DeliberativeDistortions.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/deliberative-distortions-homogenization-polarization-and-domination-in-small-group-deliberations/)): With Robert Luskin, Kyu Hahn, and James Fishkin. The British Journal of Political Science. 52(3), 1205–1225, 2022. Across 2,601 group-issue pairs in 21 Deliberative Polls, we test whether discussion routinely homogenizes or polarizes attitudes, or shifts them toward those of socially advantaged participants. We find no strong or routine pattern of these distortions; the modest patterns include some homogenization and moderation. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_distortions/).
- [Steadier, Not Closer: What Response Error Can Explain in Deliberative Polls](https://gsood.com/research/papers/SteadierNotCloser.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/steadier-not-closer-separating-convergence-from-crystallization-in-deliberative-polls/)): When survey respondents give more consistent answers after deliberation, the spread of their answers can shrink even if their opinions remain as far apart as before. The paper examines this possibility in a reanalysis of Deliberative Polls. In a sensitivity analysis, a before-to-after reliability ratio of 0.91 would account for the average observed convergence. Evidence from three UK Health attitude scales is mixed and does not establish whether reliability changed across the full sample. Links: [Manuscript source](https://github.com/finite-sample/dp_steadier_not_closer/tree/main/ms), [Source Data](https://github.com/soodoku/dp_data).
- [What Future for Kirkuk? Evidence from a deliberative intervention](https://gsood.com/research/papers/kirkuk.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/what-future-for-kirkuk-evidence-from-a-deliberative-intervention/)): With Ian O'Flynn, Jalal Mistaffa, and Nahwi Saeed. Democratization. 26(7), 1299–1317, 2019. A survey and deliberative field experiment examine young, educated Kirkuk residents' preferences for governing their divided society. Participants support an equal say for ethnic groups, and informed deliberation broadens support for regional autonomy without substantially changing support for equal say. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/kirkuk/), [Supporting Information](https://gsood.com/research/papers/kirkuk_si.pdf).

### Information Environment
- [Not News: Provision of Apolitical News in the British News Media](https://gsood.com/research/papers/not_news_uk.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/not-news-provision-of-apolitical-news-in-the-british-news-media/)): With Suriyan Laohaprapanon. We classify roughly 5.4 million webpages from 276 British news outlets to estimate how much coverage concerns topics outside public affairs. A classifier trained using article URL categories and checked against hand coding estimates that about 39% of articles are apolitical news. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/uk_not_news).
- [Strength in Numbers: Multiple Measures of Media Ideology](https://gsood.com/research/papers/multiple_measures.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/strength-in-numbers-multiple-measures-of-media-ideology/)): With Philip Habel. We combine text-based and audience-based measures of British news outlets' ideology. Parliamentary speeches, party manifestos, and Twitter following patterns provide complementary information about ideological position and differences between measurement approaches. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/uk_media_ideology/).
- [Measuring Agendas and Positions on Agendas](https://gsood.com/research/papers/issue_ideology.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/measuring-agendas-and-positions-on-agendas/)): With Andrew Guess. We distinguish which issues news outlets cover from the positions they take within those issues. A supervised topic model and congressional-speech-based slant measures reveal systematic differences across 255 news programs on 50 television channels. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/issue_ideology/).
- [notnews: Predict the Type of News Based on Story Text and URL](https://github.com/notnews/notnews) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/notnews-predict-the-type-of-news-based-on-story-text-and-url/)): With Suriyan Laohaprapanon. A Python library for classifying news by topic and distinguishing hard from soft news. It offers URL-pattern rules, trained US and UK text models, and optional language-model classification through Python and command-line interfaces.
- [Unreadable News: How Readable is American News?](https://github.com/notnews/unreadable_news) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/unreadable-news-how-readable-is-american-news/)): With Lucas Shen. We compare readability across New York Times articles and CNN, NPR, and MSNBC transcripts. The analysis examines variation across outlets and over time as one possible barrier to accessing political information.
- [Follow Your Ideology: Measuring Media Ideology on Social Networks](https://gsood.com/research/papers/mediabias.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/follow-your-ideology-a-measure-of-ideological-location-of-media-sources/)): With Pablo Barberá. We estimate the ideological positions of more than 2,300 media sources using the following patterns of politically interested social-media users. Comparisons with content-based measures support the approach, and applications examine journalists' ideology and ideological diversity within outlets.
- [The Supply of Media Slant Across Outlets and Demand for Slant Within Outlets: Evidence from US Presidential Campaign News](https://gsood.com/research/papers/hr.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-supply-of-media-slant-across-outlets-and-demand-for-slant-within-outlets-evidence-from-us-presidential-campaign-news/)): With Marcel Garz, Daniel Stone, and Justin Wallace. European Journal of Political Economy, 63, 101877, 2020. We study presidential campaign horse-race headlines across six online news outlets in 2012 and 2016. Headlines tend to favor their outlets' typical readers, but within-outlet engagement provides little evidence that readers prefer congenial headlines and somewhat more evidence of demand for uncongenial ones. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/horse_race).
- [Don't Expose Yourself: Discretionary Exposure to Political Information](https://gsood.com/research/papers/selexp.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/don-t-expose-yourself-discretionary-exposure-to-political-information/)): With Yphtach Lelkes. Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Politics. 2018. We reconsider claims that greater choice over political information increases knowledge gaps and polarization. The review questions the premise of widening knowledge gaps and finds that the evidence connecting selective exposure to polarization is more limited and nuanced than common accounts suggest. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/selexp), [Categorizing the Content of Domains](https://github.com/themains/piedomains), [Measuring Selective Exposure](http://gojiberries.io/measuring-selective-exposure-a-selective-measure-of-selective-exposure/), [The Fairest of All](http://gojiberries.io/the-fairest-of-them-all/).
- [The Good NYT: Provision of Apolitical News in the New York Times](https://github.com/notnews/good_nyt) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-good-nyt-provision-of-apolitical-news-in-the-new-york-times/)): We use the annotated New York Times corpus from 1987 to 2007 to study the mix of public-affairs and apolitical coverage. The project also develops analyses of geographic focus using article metadata and location fields.
- [Hard News: The Softening of Network Television News](https://gsood.com/research/papers/us_news.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/hard-news-the-softening-of-network-television-news/)): With Daniel Weitzel. A coded sample of more than 5,000 network television news segments from 1968 to 2019 documents changes in political content and geographic focus. Coverage unrelated to politics increases over time, and local news becomes a substantially larger share in the later years. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/hard_news/).
- [Partisan Imbalance in Politifact?](https://github.com/notnews/politifact) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/partisan-imbalance-in-politifact/)): We combine scraped PolitiFact ratings with independently coded party affiliations to examine differences in scrutiny and ratings across parties. The analysis distinguishes how often statements are checked from the average rating among the statements selected for checking.
- [Top News! URLs from News Feeds of Major National News Sites (2022-)](https://github.com/notnews/top_news) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/top-news-urls-from-news-feeds-of-major-national-news-sites-2022/)): With Derek Willis. A scheduled collector archives URLs from major news sources for studying news production. The repository contains source-specific URL collections and links to historical full-text releases, whose coverage differs from the current collections.
- [CNN Transcripts 2000--2025](https://github.com/notnews/cnn_transcripts/) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/cnn-transcripts-2000-2025/)): A corpus and scraper for CNN transcripts spanning 2000 through March 2025, with program names, dates, times, and transcript text. The repository documents collection across versions of CNN's site and links to research-access data on Harvard Dataverse. Links: [Internet Archive TV captions](https://github.com/notnews/archive_news_cc), [Vanderbilt TV news abstracts](https://github.com/notnews/vandy_tv_news_abstracts), [NBC / MSNBC transcripts](https://github.com/notnews/nbc_transcripts).
- [What and Who is on Network Television?](https://github.com/notnews/tv_schedules) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/what-and-who-is-on-network-television/)): We combine television schedules with program metadata to study changes in genres and the race and gender composition of casts and production teams. The repository includes collection scripts, data, and figures describing these trends.
- [Working Women on Indian TV](https://github.com/notnews/working_women_on_tv) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/working-women-on-indian-tv/)): With Asha Sood. We code employment among fictional female characters in Indian evening television soaps. In data collected in 2015 on 172 characters across 20 shows, 36.6% of working-age female characters are portrayed as working, with substantial variation across shows.
- [The Face of Crime in Prime Time: Evidence from Law and Order](https://gsood.com/research/papers/face_of_crime.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-face-of-crime-in-prime-time-evidence-from-law-and-order/)): With Daniel Trielli. We tally the coded race and gender of victims and criminals across three Law and Order series. Black characters appear at lower shares than in several historical arrest and victimization series, while women appear at higher shares among criminals than in several arrest categories. The comparisons are descriptive because the sources differ in crimes, places, and years. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/face_of_crime), [The Washington Post](https://gsood.com/research/press/LawOrderWP.pdf).

### Other
- [Problem Solving](https://gsood.com/research/papers/problem_solving.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/problem-solving/)): A practical framework for diagnosing problems: generate specific explanations, assess their plausibility, and design checks that distinguish among them. Examples show how correlations, close examination of failures, and comparisons with successful cases can help identify causes.
- [Is an Uncertain Prospect Less Preferred Than Its Worst Possible Outcome? New Evidence on the Uncertainty Effect](https://gsood.com/research/papers/uncertainty.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/is-an-uncertain-prospect-less-preferred-than-its-worst-possible-outcome-new-evidence-on-the-uncertainty-effect/)): With Doug Ahler. Two larger surveys replicate the finding that people sometimes prefer a certain option to a lottery whose worst outcome is better. Clarifying the guarantee reduces the effect, while expressing the lottery as natural frequencies or using monetary choices eliminates it in these experiments. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/uncertainty).
- [Description Invariance in Risky-Choice Framing: Evidence from Five Survey Experiments](https://gsood.com/research/papers/prospect_theory.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/description-invariance-in-risky-choice-framing/)): With John Protzko and Jon Krosnick. Five archival survey experiments test whether equivalent gain and loss descriptions change risky choices. All 23 contrasts show the classic framing direction, but explicitly stating the certain outcome removes much of the gap, suggesting that inferences from incomplete descriptions matter alongside gain and loss labels. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/prospect_theory).
- [Is Cynicism Taken as Evidence of Political Sophistication?](https://gsood.com/research/papers/sophisticated_cynic.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/is-cynicism-taken-as-evidence-of-political-sophistication/)): With Alexander G. Theodoridis. In a two-arm comparison in the 2020 Cooperative Election Study, 711 respondents rated one of two tweets. Both said the system rewards bad behavior; one said politics attracts good people, the other bad people. The bad-people tweet scored 6.2 points lower in perceived sophistication on a 0–100 scale (95% CI: −9.4 to −3.0). Covariate adjustment and survey weighting preserve the negative difference. A causal interpretation requires random assignment within the rating sample; the original questionnaire and randomization program are unavailable. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/sophisticated_cynic).
- [Mixed Signals: Movie Quality Assessments Across Platforms](https://github.com/soodoku/mixed_signals) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/mixed-signals-movie-quality-assessments-across-platforms/)): We compare movie ratings across platforms using data on 16,319 American films released between 1950 and 2020. Among platforms with sufficient coverage, average ratings are only moderately correlated, revealing substantial differences in assessments of the same films.
- [Americans' Attitudes Toward The Affordable Care Act: Would Better Public Understanding Increase or Decrease Favorability?](https://gsood.com/research/papers/ACAKnowledgeFavorability.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/americans-attitudes-toward-the-affordable-care-act-would-better-public-understanding-increase-or-decrease-favorability/)): With Wendy Gross, Tobias Stark, Jon Krosnick, Josh Pasek, Trevor Tompson, Jennifer Agiesta, and Dennis Junius. Surveys from 2010 and 2012 find substantial misunderstanding of the Affordable Care Act despite support for many of its provisions. The analysis estimates that fuller understanding could increase support for the law; this is a modeled implication, rather than a demonstrated effect of an information campaign. Links: [Forbes](https://gsood.com/research/press/ForbesHealthcare.pdf), [Pacific Standard](https://gsood.com/research/press/PSMagHealthcare.pdf), [The Dish](https://gsood.com/research/press/TheDishHealthcare.pdf).
- [Americans' Attitudes toward the Affordable Care Act: What Role Do Beliefs Play?](https://gsood.com/research/papers/ACA_beliefs_attitudes.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/americans-attitudes-toward-the-affordable-care-act-what-role-do-beliefs-play/)): With Gabriel Miao Li, Josh Pasek, Jon Krosnick, Tobias Stark, Jennifer Agiesta, Trevor Tompson, and Wendy Gross. The ANNALS of the American Academy of Political and Social Science, 700(1), 41–54, 2022. We examine whether Americans evaluate the Affordable Care Act through beliefs about its individual provisions. Despite partisan disagreement, both Democrats' and Republicans' evaluations are associated with what they believe the law does and how confident they are in those beliefs.
- [Revisiting a Natural Experiment: Do Legislators With Daughters Vote More Liberally on Women's Issues?](https://gsood.com/research/papers/daughters.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/revisiting-a-natural-experiment-do-legislators-with-daughters-vote-more-liberally-on-women-s-issues/)): With Don Green, Oliver Hyman-Metzger, and Michelle Zee. Journal of Political Economy Microeconomics, 1(3), 506–516, 2023. We revisit evidence that legislators with daughters vote more liberally on women's issues, extending the analysis to eight congresses before and eight after the original study period. We find no daughters effect in either extension, challenging the explanation that later party polarization alone erased the relationship. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/daughters), [Supporting Information](https://gsood.com/research/papers/daughters_si.pdf), [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2023-05-daughters-politicians-votes-women-issues.html).
- [Extreme Recall: Which Politicians Come to Mind?](https://gsood.com/research/papers/extreme_recall.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/extreme-recall-which-politicians-come-to-mind/)): With Daniel Weitzel. Journal of Elections, Public Opinion and Parties, 35(2), 247–268, 2025. Two surveys nearly a decade apart show that people's images of political parties center on a few prominent national figures, with more extreme politicians recalled more often. Television news coverage is associated with which politicians come to mind. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/notnews/extreme_recall_2023), [Extreme Recall](https://github.com/notnews/extreme_recall).

## Political Economy of India
- [Do Namesakes Confuse Voters? Evidence from Six Decades of Indian Elections](https://gsood.com/research/papers/candidate_namesakes.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/do-namesakes-confuse-voters/)): Indian ballots often list minor independents who share a leading candidate's name. Across 570,241 Lok Sabha and assembly candidate records from 1962 to 2026, independents named like a leading candidate place 7.8 percentile points higher among their contest's independents than other independents (SE 1.4), while those named like a minor-party candidate gain nothing detectable. The votes involved are few: counting only votes attributable to the name, namesakes exceeded the winning margin in 12 of 57,166 contests (95% range 4–18). The premium shrank after candidate photographs were added to voting machines in 2015, but placebo break dates produce declines of the same size. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/in-rolls/candidate_namesakes), [Indian election results, 2023–2026, in TCPD's layout](https://github.com/in-rolls/eci_results).
- [The Limits of Electoral Gender Quotas in Rural Local Bodies](https://gsood.com/research/papers/quota_raj.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-limits-of-electoral-gender-quotas-in-rural-local-bodies/)): With Varun Karekurve-Ramachandra. Across more than 34,000 rural local bodies, prior reservation produces small or inconsistent short-run gains in women's success in subsequently open seats. Phone audits document extensive male mediation of access to women elected under quotas, a pattern consistent with, but not proof of, proxy governance limiting independent political careers. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/in-rolls/quota_representation), [Governance](https://github.com/in-rolls/quota_governance), [Public spending](https://github.com/in-rolls/quota_spending), [PDS](https://github.com/in-rolls/quota_pds), [Marriage](https://github.com/in-rolls/quota_marriage), [VoxDev](https://voxdev.org/topic/institutions-political-economy/no-representation-without-reservation-long-term-limits-gender).
- [Female Reservation and the Qualifications of Local Elected Officials in India](https://gsood.com/research/papers/quota_elite_quality.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-effect-of-gender-quotas-on-some-qualities-of-elites/)): Schooling differences under women's reservation follow distinct patterns across offices and settings. Published village-head studies and our northern village-head estimates show deficits among reserved-seat winners; Kerala's village ward members and councillors in Mumbai and Delhi show no consistent deficit, although the urban estimates do not establish equivalence. We synthesize these groups separately, rather than treating a single overall average as the main finding. Reserved-seat winners are more likely to report no occupation in the village, block and city offices with occupation records, but face fewer pending criminal charges in Mumbai and Delhi. The records do not establish effects on governing performance. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/in-rolls/quota_elite_quality).
- [The Older Half: Spousal Age Gap in India](https://github.com/in-rolls/spousal_age_gap) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/the-older-half-spousal-age-gap-in-india/)): With Suriyan Laohaprapanon. Using electoral-roll records for nearly 70 million couples across Indian states and union territories, we describe spousal age differences. Husbands are generally older, with an average gap of about 4.1 years and substantial variation across states and spouses' ages. Links: [Indian electoral rolls](https://github.com/in-rolls/electoral_rolls).
- [Unlanded: Distribution of Land in Bihar](https://gsood.com/research/papers/land.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/unlanded-distribution-of-land-in-bihar/)): With Lucas Shen. Digitized land records from Bihar reveal concentrated ownership and substantial disparities by gender, religion, and caste. Men make up 76.5% of landowners, and Muslims, Scheduled Castes, and Extremely Backward Classes are underrepresented; the study measures ownership rather than operational agricultural holdings. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/in-rolls/land).
- [Indian Electoral Rolls: Data and Extraction Tools](https://github.com/in-rolls/electoral_rolls) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/indian-electoral-rolls/)): With Atul Dhingra. Scripts and linked tools collect and parse Indian electoral rolls published as PDFs by state election authorities. The project provides a foundation for research using recorded names, ages, gender labels, family relationships, and electoral geography. Links: [Searchable-roll parser](https://github.com/in-rolls/electoral_rolls_parse_searchable), [Scanned-roll parser](https://github.com/in-rolls/electoral_rolls_parse_unsearchable).

## Missing Women
- [Women and Men on Urban Streets: Evidence from Crowdsourced Photographs in 101 Cities](https://gsood.com/research/papers/missing_women_global.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/missing-women-on-global-streets/)): Across 28,794 ground-level photographs from 101 cities, women accounted for 36.0% of classified pedestrian sightings. The share ranged from 16.0% in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan to 49.4% in Europe and Central Asia. The paper compares the photographs with human counts and local population records. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/geosensing/missing_women_crowdsourced_photos_multicountry).
- [Measuring Women’s and Men’s Presence on Urban Streets: Evidence from Google Street View in 98 Cities](https://gsood.com/research/papers/street_presence_98_cities.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/google-street-view-98-cities/)): The study sampled 98,000 street and walking-route locations in 98 cities and obtained 9,997 Google Street View images from 82 cities. Among sightings the model could classify, women accounted for 28.8% of pedestrians and 5.4% of two-wheeler riders. The model could not classify 66% of all sightings. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/geosensing/mw_streetview).
- [Missing women on Indian streets](https://gsood.com/research/papers/missing_women.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/missing-women-on-indian-streets/)): With Varun Karekurve-Ramachandra. Randomly sampled streets in four Indian cities reveal a large gender imbalance in public space: women account for 12% to 16% of observed adults. Comparisons with residential populations and time-use data suggest that much of the gap arises because women leave home less often and make fewer trips. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/geosensing/streetscope), [Marginal Revolution](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2026/07/missing-women-on-indian-streets.html), [Watching the Wheels (podcast)](https://music.amazon.co.uk/podcasts/37424666-0994-4d1b-9703-ae037bc10d9d/episodes/e3305856-5472-47be-8fb8-648470cb6f43/watching-the-wheels-ep-1-where-have-all-the-women-gone), [The Wire](https://thewire.in/women/70-of-women-in-mumbai-navi-mumbai-missing-from-the-cities-streets-finds-study), [Invisible Women (Caroline Criado Perez)](https://newsletter.carolinecriadoperez.com/p/pervert-glasses-and-missing-women).
- [Who Eats in Delhi Street-Food Videos?](https://github.com/soodoku/mw_youtube) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/delhi-street-food-videos/)): In 450 randomly sampled frames from 30 Delhi street-food videos published in 2025, women accounted for 13.5% of apparent diner sightings and 16.1% of all sightings with classifiable gender, after weighting each video equally. A person with a serving of food in hand or in front of them counts as a diner, as does someone sharing a meal.
- [Son Bias in the US: Evidence from Business Names](https://gsood.com/research/papers/sonny_side.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/son-bias-in-the-us-evidence-from-business-names/)): With Walter Guillioli. We compare businesses named with 'son' or 'sons' and 'daughter' or 'daughters' using state business registries. Across 40 states, the median ratio is 12 to 1, with limitations in registry searches making the analysis a conservative accounting of the imbalance. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/soodoku/sonny_side).
- [Which Women Are Missing? Adult Sex Ratio By Last Name](https://github.com/in-rolls/last_sex) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/which-women-are-missing-adult-sex-ratio-by-last-name/)): With Suriyan Laohaprapanon. We use Indian electoral-roll records for more than 35 million people to estimate adult sex ratios by surname. The analysis describes variation that state-level averages can obscure, using recorded electoral-roll gender labels.
- [Women and Men on Delhi’s Streets: Evidence from Field Photographs, 2016–2017](https://github.com/geosensing/mw_survey_delhi) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/missing-women-on-the-streets/)): Reviewers counted people in 1,958 street photographs taken at 196 Delhi locations between November 2016 and January 2017. Women accounted for 18.5% of sightings across the photographs. Field collection departed from the planned random sample, limiting what the photographs can establish about Delhi as a whole.
- [Epic Children: Sex Ratio of Children of Key Characters in Epics](https://github.com/soodoku/epic_children) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/epic-children-sex-ratio-of-children-of-key-characters-in-epics/)): A dataset records sons and daughters attributed to key figures across epic and mythological traditions. It documents large differences in the visibility of named sons and daughters, with source and family-structure information for interpreting the counts.
- [Missing Daughters of Indian Politicians](https://github.com/in-rolls/missing_daughters) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/missing-daughters-of-indian-politicians/)): We use official biographies of members of India's 12th through 17th Lok Sabhas to examine the sex ratio of politicians' children. The project compares recorded sons and daughters to assess whether the imbalance observed in the wider population also appears among political elites.

## Cricket

### Analysis and Ratings
- [Fairly Random: The Effect of Winning the Toss on Winning the Match](https://gsood.com/research/papers/cricket_paper.pdf) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/fairly-random-the-effect-of-winning-the-toss-on-winning-the-match/)): With Apoorva Lal, Derek Willis, and Avidit Acharya. Journal of Sports Analytics. 2023. We use cricket's coin toss to estimate the advantage of choosing whether to bat or bowl first. The estimated effect on winning is negligible in daytime international limited-overs matches, but about 3.3 percentage points in day-night matches and 4.9 points in Tests; rain-adjusted matches show no statistically distinguishable effect. Links: [Replication Materials](https://github.com/outside-edge/fairly_random), [Fairly Random: Impact of Winning the Toss on the Probability of Winning](https://github.com/outside-edge/toss_up), [arXiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.08753), [ESPN: How much does the toss really matter?](https://gsood.com/research/press/CricketESPN.pdf), [ESPN: Why replacing the toss with an auction is the fair thing to do](https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/why-replacing-the-toss-with-an-auction-is-the-fair-thing-to-do-1277744), [python-espncricinfo](https://github.com/outside-edge/python-espncricinfo), [Cricket data and collection scripts](https://github.com/outside-edge/get_cricket_data).
- [Side Order: Rating International Cricket Teams](https://outside-edge.github.io/side_order/) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/elo-ratings-of-international-cricket-teams-by-format/)): With Derek Willis. Weekly Elo ratings track men's international teams separately in Tests, one-day internationals, and Twenty20 internationals. Monthly histories are available to download, alongside ratings from four other methods. Links: [Source code](https://github.com/outside-edge/side_order), [The Hindu](https://gsood.com/research/press/EloDutch.pdf), [View ratings](https://outside-edge.github.io/side_order/#read-the-ratings), [Download data](https://outside-edge.github.io/side_order/docs/data.html).
- [Player Value: Rating International Cricketers](https://outside-edge.github.io/player_value/) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/war-ratings-for-cricketers/)): With Derek Willis. Player rankings use five years of lineups and match outcomes to estimate how playing strength varies across cricketers. Separate tables cover men's and women's Tests, one-day internationals, and Twenty20 internationals. Links: [Source code](https://github.com/outside-edge/player_value).
- [Which IPL Players Go On to Play International Cricket?](https://outside-edge.github.io/national_selection/) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/ipl-international-debuts/)): For Indian Premier League players who have yet to play for a national side, the project forecasts a first international appearance in the next 12 months. Historical forecasts show how well IPL performance predicts debuts. Links: [Source code](https://github.com/outside-edge/national_selection).
- [IPL Auction Prices and Player Performance](https://github.com/outside-edge/ipl_auction) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/ipl-auction-prices/)): The study compares Indian Premier League auction prices with players' subsequent batting and bowling performances. Ball-by-ball records link each purchase to an estimate of wins above replacement.

### Data and Software
- [ESPNcricinfo Python Client](https://outside-edge.github.io/python-espncricinfo/) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/espncricinfo-python-client/)): With Derek Willis. A Python package for retrieving match, series, season, team, and player records from ESPNcricinfo. Links: [Source code](https://github.com/outside-edge/python-espncricinfo).
- [Cricket Match Data: More Than 43,000 Matches](https://github.com/outside-edge/get_cricket_data) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/cricket-match-data/)): Match-level records collected from ESPNcricinfo, with the scripts used to retrieve and parse the scorecards. Links: [Download CSV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/outside-edge/get_cricket_data/master/data/final_output.csv).
- [Cricket Grounds and Jurisdictions](https://github.com/outside-edge/cricket_grounds) ([page](https://gsood.com/research/cricket-grounds-and-jurisdictions/)): A dated lookup table connects ESPNcricinfo ground IDs to cricket jurisdictions. Match dates determine which jurisdiction applies when a ground's affiliation has changed. Links: [Download CSV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/outside-edge/cricket_grounds/main/grounds.csv).
